title: Google's Negative Cash Flow and the AI Capex Reckoning | The Weekly Wrap
summary: Eisman sees AI investors becoming more demanding about cash flow, competitive moats and rising capex. He contrasts strong equipment demand with pressure on hyperscaler finances and software valuations, reviews several earnings reports, and explains why banks do not diversify his AI exposure. He also describes funding shorts.
assessment: Full transcript reviewed. Empirical claims without inspected primary outcome evidence remain unresolved; guest claims are separate from Eisman attribution. Primary outcome verification is incomplete for claims marked unresolved; these are not adverse accuracy grades.
speaker_map_notes: Steve Eisman hosts the episode; guest turns are inferred from introductions and conversational context.
framework_points: Evaluate earnings quality by removing investment gains.
For long-cycle equipment suppliers, orders and backlog can matter more than quarterly EPS.
Separate an operating beat from the market's expectations for guidance.
Look through bank profits to their AI financing exposure.
tools_and_charts: Alphabet adjusted EPS, cloud growth and free cash flow
transcript_cautions: The caption substitutes cesspool for SaaS-apocalypse during the Equifax discussion.
The private-credit sentence appears to omit not before until next year; surrounding context clearly describes future refinancing risk.
